newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks edge down by lunch awaiting bank data.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks edge down by lunch awaiting bank data.

text.p: Thai stocks fell by the lunch break on Thursday in a slow session as many investors remained sidelined ahead of central bank economic data due later and the resumption of Finance One shares on Friday, analysts said.
The SET Index lost 0.95 points in the morning going into the the break at 561.89. The SET 50 was unchanged at 40.69. Turnover was a meagre 983 million baht.

Most economic numbers have already been announced but investors are eager to see the central bank's foreign reserves as attacks on the baht earlier this year prompted Bank of Thailand intervention to defend the currency, analysts said.

"Most economic factors have been absorbed following their release earlier this week ... but investors want to see the international reserves to see how much the central bank spent in defending the baht earlier this year," said Somchai Trairattanapirom, vice president at Sitca.
Maintenance of reserves at around the $38 billion level will be positive for the market, traders said.

There were nerves in the market surrounding Friday's resumption of trading in stocks of troubled finance firm Finance One Plc after a three month suspension and the collapse of a planned merger, analysts said.
With the shares expected to begin trading at well below their 10 baht par value, compared to a last trading price of 23.75 in February, traders said the stock may move the market lower.
Speculators gambling on the afternoon's data moved in for banking stocks prior to the break and helped pare most earlier losses, traders said.
Krung Thai Bank Plc added 0.25 baht to 28.50, Siam City Bank Plc added 0.75 to 15.50. Finance and securities firm Dhana Siam Plc topped the active list and lost one to 19.25.
